original_metadata.title: All intrinsic characteristic classes of a smooth Lie algebroid pull back functorially along every transverse smooth map, without a connectivity condition on its fibers
original_metadata.author: Pedro Frejlich
original_metadata.source_title: Morita Invariance of Intrinsic Characteristic Classes of Lie Algebroids
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The adjoint representation up to homotopy of an inverse-image Lie algebroid is not just the pullback adjoint bundle. The proof constructs a compatible connection that splits off the doubled vertical bundle with matching metric connections and identifies the resulting graded Chern-Simons forms. Transverse normal forms and graph factorization then extend the exact identity from submersions to arbitrary transverse maps.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The complete main proof and all new Proposition3 connection construction were read, along with the exact graded-adjoint and secondary-class definitions. For a surjective submersion the author constructs horizontal/vertical splittings, compatible metrics and a four-part connection with the Ehresmann curvature correction. He computes all basic-connection components, obtains matching metric vertical subconnections and pulls the graded Chern-Simons expression back exactly. A prior transverse normal-form theorem handles closed embeddings; factorization through the graph then gives every transverse smooth map. This does not assume that the adjoint representation itself simply pulls back, and no fiber-connectivity condition is imposed. Primary/secondary characteristic-class properties and the normal-form theorem are established cited background.

original_metadata.statement_scope: The full unnumbered Main Theorem: for a smooth Lie algebroid A on M and a smooth map phi:N->M transverse to its anchor, char(phi^! A)=phi^* char(A) in all odd intrinsic characteristic-class degrees. Retain the usual inverse-image Lie algebroid and induced morphism on cohomology. No surjectivity or fiber connectivity is assumed for the final phi. The weak-Morita invariance follows through the explicitly described pullback comparison, but is not counted as another item. This is not a statement for arbitrary nontransverse maps.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The complete original unnumbered main functoriality theorem and every author proof step are retained for any smooth transverse map. The adjoint/graded Chern-Simons definitions, full four-part horizontal/vertical compatible-connection recipe with Ehresmann-curvature correction, all basic-connection components and matching metric vertical subconnections are supplied as new core. The source normal-form theorem for transverse closed embeddings and primary/secondary-class properties remain cited standard prerequisites. Graph factorization then gives the unrestricted transverse map. Neither surjectivity nor fiber connectivity is required for the selected final map, and weak-Morita invariance is not separately counted.
